\newcommand{\PVTFailSentence}{Across the 25 designs returned by the four main methods that pass at TT but fail the grid, 59\% of the 297 failing conditions are at the low supply (1.62\,V) and 23 of the 25 designs fail at least one low-supply condition; failing conditions by corner are SF 65, FS 65, FF 60, SS 59, TT 48 and by temperature $-40\,^\circ$C 111, 125\,$^\circ$C 109, 27\,$^\circ$C 77.}
\newcommand{\SpectraFailSentence}{SPECTRA fails 24 of its runs on the common tasks, 7 of them robust. In these robust failures the PVT loop consumed a median of 141 of the 600 condition-evaluations, and in 4 of them the worst-case violation did not decrease between successive full verifications; because the loop has no early exit, such runs return to the LLM with budget for few edits (median 12 LLM calls used). Its nominal failures used a median of 12 LLM calls. All primary-endpoint tasks on which the AnalogCoder-style agent does better than SPECTRA are comparators, latches, LDOs, op-amps, op-amp applications, Schmitt triggers, TIAs.}

\newcommand{\MCSentence}{Under 100-sample mismatch Monte Carlo at TT, the mean yield of the PVT-verified seed-0 designs is SPECTRA 87\% (15 designs, 12 with yield $\geq$90\%); SPECTRA-min 80\% (10 designs, 6 with yield $\geq$90\%); the AnalogCoder-style agent 85\% (15 designs, 11 with yield $\geq$90\%); Gen+TPE 88\% (6 designs, 4 with yield $\geq$90\%); SPECTRA w/o PVT-aware refinement 95\% (7 designs, 5 with yield $\geq$90\%); Gen+TPE-full 98\% (7 designs, 6 with yield $\geq$90\%).}
